focus: A3b v2 port specs for the five hard plugins (sentinel, skill-advisor, spec-gate, goal, sk-vision) and resolution of the five open P0s

label: The 2.0.32 v2 plugin Context exposes app/location/options plus 18 domains and has NO client and NO tui member; SessionDomain is a closed Pick of 16 SessionApi methods that omits messages, so ctx.client.session.messages (sentinel:79, spec-gate:90) has no typed v2 equivalent at all - a missing capability, not a signature change.

v2 message list carries no parts: GET /api/session/{sessionID}/message -> SessionMessagesResponse whose data is an array of Session.Message.Info, an anyOf of 11 variants (AgentSelected, ModelSelected, LocationSwitched, User, Synthetic, System, Skill, Shell, Assistant, Compaction, Idle) none of which defines parts and none of which wraps an info object; assistant text is content[].text and user text is User.text, so sentinel:56/88 and spec-gate:102 silently yield null on v2.

promptAsync parity confirmed: ctx.session.prompt (prompt IS in the SessionDomain Pick) maps to POST /api/session/{sessionID}/prompt taking {id?,text,files?,agents?,skills?,metadata?} and returning 200 {data: Session.Inbox.User}; SessionInbox.Delivery = steer|queue proves the call enqueues into the session inbox and returns, i.e. async semantics, so opencode-goal's continuation gate can be rewritten as ctx.session.prompt({sessionID,text,delivery:'queue'}).

No typed toast on v2: Context has no tui, EventDomain is Pick<EventApi,'subscribe'> with no emit, the 2.0.32 OpenAPI document has no /api/tui route and no Tui/Toast schema, and RpcRegistration.events.emit only emits for a definition the plugin itself registered - so sk-vision's input.client.tui.showToast has no direct v2 port; the only residual channel is a host tui RPC id behind POST /api/rpc/{rpcID}/{method}, whose method vocabulary is unread.

The spec gate reads the user prompt through ctx.session.hook('prompt') -> SessionPrompt {sessionID,messageID,prompt:PromptInput.Prompt,metadata?,delivery}, which replaces both the experimental.chat.system.transform input (which carries no prompt field) and the client.session.messages fallback; injection moves to ctx.session.hook('context') -> SessionContext {sessionID,model,system:SystemPart[],messages:Message[],options,agent,tools} where output.system.push becomes system.push, removing the cross-hook session-key coupling; request kind is NOT on context but on the separate SessionModelRequest hook as SessionRequestKind = primary|compaction|title|generate.

Lifecycle on 2.0.32: Plugin.setup returns Cleanup|void, every hook() and transform() returns Promise<Registration> where Registration is exactly {dispose()}, and registration.d.ts ships NO Reload interface (closing the carried P2); reload is per domain via tool.reload()/command.reload()/skill.reload(). Module-level caches must be created inside setup and reset in the returned Cleanup, and skill-advisor's server.instance.disposed/global.disposed reset pair has no v2 replacement because Cleanup IS the signal.

command.execute.before has no v2 hook: CommandDomain is Pick<CommandApi,'list'> & {transform,reload}. The v2 equivalent is to own the command via ctx.command.transform(editor => editor.add({name,description?,execute(input)})) with CommandInvocation {sessionID,prompt:PromptInput.Prompt,delivery}. This is a semantic change for sk-vision, which on v1 observes commands it does not own and would on v2 have to register the vision command itself (name collision instead of observation).

Uniform dual-shape export: Plugin is exactly {id, setup}, and all five hard plugins export a bare async function for v1, so export default Object.assign(v1Factory,{id,setup}) is callable for v1 and id/setup-bearing for v2; whether the v2 loader reads those two keys structurally or applies a shape test that rejects a callable-with-extras is unproven and POST /api/plugin/check is the single call that settles it.

Options and host detection move: v1 plugins take (ctx, rawOptions) while v2 setup receives one Context whose per-plugin options are context.options (Readonly<Record<string,any>>) and whose context.app is {name,version,channel} - so ctx.app.version is a real host-derived discriminator that weakens the case for the env-gated ORCA_OPENCODE_PLUGIN_API selector.

Tool registration becomes a transform: v1's tool:{...} object literal maps to ctx.tool.transform(editor => editor.add({...})) with Info.execute(input, ToolContext{signal,progress,...}) and ToolEditor.list/get/add/update/remove; Info.Input is constrained to Tool.ValueSchema<any> from @opencode/schema/tool, which is not vendored in the pack, so whether a v1 zod-or-JSON-schema args passes that constraint stays unresolved.
